title: BRACHYOLMIA TYPE 4 WITH MILD EPIPHYSEAL AND METAPHYSEAL CHANGES

relationships.phenotype: BRACHYOLMIA TYPE 4 WITH MILD EPIPHYSEAL AND METAPHYSEAL CHANGES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that brachyolmia type 4 with mild epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes (BCYM4) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PAPSS2 gene (603005) on chromosome 10q23.2-q23.31.

checks.claim: Brachyolmia type 4 with mild epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes (BCYM4) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PAPSS2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: one patient was homozygous for IVS3+2delT, and the other two were compound heterozygotes for c.616-634del19 (p.V206SfsX9) and c.1309-1310delAG (p.R437GfsX19)
checks.explanation: The abstract shows that homozygous and compound heterozygous PAPSS2 mutations cause AR brachyolmia. It never uses the name 'brachyolmia type 4 with mild epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes'; it only says the epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes were variable.

checks.claim: The PAPSS2 gene is located on chromosome 10q23.2-q23.31.
checks.evidence_quote: identified its disease gene, PAPSS2 (phosphoadenosine-phosphosulfate synthetase 2)
checks.explanation: The abstract doesn't give the chromosomal location, but under the task rules a gene's location is standard nomenclature that restates the paper's gene.

paragraphs.text: Brachyolmia type 4 with mild epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes (BCYM4) is an autosomal recessive skeletal dysplasia. Its features include short-trunk short stature (Miyake et al., 2012), platyspondyly, and mild changes in the epiphyses and metaphyses (Ahmad et al., 1998). The disorder is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the gene that encodes PAPS synthase-2 (Miyake et al., 2012). This ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase activates inorganic sulfate to 3-prime-phosphoadenosine 5-prime-phosphosulfate (PAPS), the universal sulfate donor (Faiyaz ul Haque et al., 1998). PAPSS2 deficiency was also reported in a girl with premature pubarche, very low DHEA sulfate levels and androgen excess (Noordam et al., 2009).

checks.claim: BCYM4 is an autosomal recessive skeletal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified PAPSS2 as the disease gene for an AR brachyolmia.
checks.explanation: The paper calls the disorder autosomal recessive (AR) brachyolmia, and brachyolmia is described as a skeletal dysplasia.

checks.claim: BCYM4 features include short-trunk short stature.
checks.evidence_quote: The six patients had short-trunk short stature that became conspicuous during childhood with normal intelligence and facies.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: BCYM4 features include platyspondyly.
checks.evidence_quote: platyspondyly with irregular end plates and narrowed joint spaces
checks.explanation: Platyspondyly is reported on radiographs.

checks.claim: BCYM4 features include mild changes in the epiphyses and metaphyses.
checks.evidence_quote: Radiographs demonstrated delayed epiphyseal ossification at the hips and knees
checks.explanation: The paper calls the metaphyseal abnormalities mild ('Mild metaphyseal abnormalities were seen predominantly at hips and knees'). It reports delayed epiphyseal ossification but does not call the epiphyseal changes mild.

checks.claim: BCYM4 is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the gene encoding PAPS synthase-2 (PAPSS2).
checks.evidence_quote: We further examined three patients with similar brachyolmia phenotypes (two Japanese and a Korean) and also identified loss of function mutations in PAPSS2
checks.explanation: The paper reports loss-of-function PAPSS2 mutations as the cause.

checks.claim: PAPS synthase-2 is an ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified two orthologous genes, ATPSK2 and Atpsk2, encoding novel ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase orthologues in the respective regions of the human and mouse genomes.
checks.explanation: The paper says ATPSK2 encodes an ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase. PAPS synthase-2 is the standard name for ATPSK2.

checks.claim: PAPS synthase-2 activates inorganic sulfate to 3-prime-phosphoadenosine 5-prime-phosphosulfate (PAPS), the universal sulfate donor.
checks.evidence_quote: ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase catalyses the metabolic activation of inorganic sulfate to PAPS, the universal donor for post-translational protein sulfation in all cell types.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: PAPSS2 deficiency was reported in a girl with premature pubarche.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified compound heterozygous mutations in the gene encoding human PAPS synthase 2 (PAPSS2) in a girl with premature pubarche
checks.explanation: The abstract describes PAPSS2 mutations in a girl with premature pubarche.

checks.claim: The girl with PAPSS2 deficiency and premature pubarche had very low DHEA sulfate levels.
checks.evidence_quote: in a girl with premature pubarche, hyperandrogenic anovulation, very low DHEAS levels, and increased androgen levels
checks.explanation: The abstract states very low DHEAS levels.

checks.claim: The girl with PAPSS2 deficiency and premature pubarche had androgen excess.
checks.evidence_quote: in a girl with premature pubarche, hyperandrogenic anovulation, very low DHEAS levels, and increased androgen levels
checks.explanation: Increased androgen levels amount to androgen excess, a term the abstract also uses in its conclusion.

paragraphs.text: Ahmad et al. (1998) described the disorder as a distinct form of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD) in a kindred from Pakistan. Miyake et al. (2012) later found PAPSS2 mutations in patients with brachyolmia.

checks.evidence_quote: with a distinct form of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD)
checks.explanation: The paper describes a distinct form of SEMD. The link to BCYM4 comes from other papers.

paragraphs.text: Ahmad et al. (1998) described a large inbred Pakistani kindred with a distinct form of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia. Affected members had short stature evident at birth, bowed lower limbs, enlarged knee joints and kyphoscoliosis. Radiographs showed platyspondyly with irregular end plates, delayed epiphyseal ossification, and mild metaphyseal abnormalities.

checks.evidence_quote: We describe a large inbred kindred from a remote area of Pakistan, comprising eight generations, with a distinct form of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD).
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.evidence_quote: platyspondyly with irregular end plates and narrowed joint spaces

paragraphs.text: Miyake et al. (2012) reported patients with autosomal recessive brachyolmia who had PAPSS2 mutations. The 6 patients had short-trunk short stature. Their radiographic features included rectangular vertebral bodies with irregular endplates and narrow intervertebral discs. Epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes of the tubular bones were variable.

paragraphs.text: The patient reported by Noordam et al. (2009) had very low DHEAS levels and increased androgen levels. In vitro, the authors coincubated human SULT2A1 with wild-type or mutant PAPSS2 proteins, and the results confirmed that the mutations were inactivating. Noordam et al. (2009) noted that sulfation converts the androgen precursor DHEA to its inactive sulfate ester, DHEAS, which prevents conversion of DHEA to an active androgen. They concluded that PAPSS2 deficiency is a monogenic adrenocortical cause of androgen excess.

paragraphs.text: Ahmad et al. (1998) reported that analysis of the pedigree of the inbred Pakistani kindred strongly suggested autosomal recessive inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) identified ATPSK2 (PAPSS2), which encodes an ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase, in the region of chromosome 10q23-q24 to which the gene for this dwarfing condition had been mapped. In the SEMD family they characterized a nonsense mutation in ATPSK2.

checks.claim: The gene for the SEMD dwarfing condition in the Pakistani kindred had been mapped to chromosome 10q23-q24.
checks.evidence_quote: We have studied a large inbred Pakistani family with a distinct form of recessively inherited spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD) and mapped a gene associated with this dwarfing condition to chromosome 10q23-24
checks.explanation: The authors themselves mapped the gene to 10q23-24 in the Pakistani family.

checks.claim: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) identified ATPSK2 (PAPSS2) in the chromosome 10q23-q24 region to which the SEMD dwarfing condition had been mapped.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified two orthologous genes, ATPSK2 and Atpsk2, encoding novel ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase orthologues in the respective regions of the human and mouse genomes.
checks.explanation: The paper places ATPSK2 in the mapped human region. ATPSK2 is now named PAPSS2.

checks.claim: ATPSK2 (PAPSS2) encodes an ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase.
checks.evidence_quote: ATPSK2 and Atpsk2, encoding novel ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase orthologues
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.evidence_quote: We characterized a nonsense mutation in ATPSK2 in the SEMD family

paragraphs.text: Miyake et al. (2012) found biallelic PAPSS2 mutations in patients with brachyolmia. One patient was homozygous and others were compound heterozygous.

checks.claim: Miyake et al. (2012) found biallelic PAPSS2 mutations in patients with brachyolmia.
checks.evidence_quote: The patients had a homozygous loss of function mutation, c.337_338insG (p.A113GfsX18).
checks.explanation: All patients carried biallelic mutations: the Turkish family was homozygous, one other patient was homozygous and two were compound heterozygous.

checks.claim: One brachyolmia patient reported by Miyake et al. (2012) was homozygous for a PAPSS2 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: one patient was homozygous for IVS3+2delT, and the other two were compound heterozygotes
checks.explanation: This is true only for the three additional (Japanese/Korean) patients. The three affected members of the Turkish family were also homozygous (c.337_338insG), so four of the six patients were homozygous, not one.

checks.claim: The other brachyolmia patients reported by Miyake et al. (2012) were compound heterozygous for PAPSS2 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: one patient was homozygous for IVS3+2delT, and the other two were compound heterozygotes
checks.explanation: Only two of the six patients were compound heterozygous. The three Turkish patients were homozygous for c.337_338insG, so 'the other patients' holds only within the second group of three.

paragraphs.text: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) identified Atpsk2 (Papss2) as the mouse ortholog of human ATPSK2 (PAPSS2). They showed that the brachymorphic (bm) mouse carries a missense mutation in the region of Atpsk2 that encodes the APS kinase activity.

checks.claim: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) identified mouse Atpsk2 (Papss2) as the ortholog of human ATPSK2 (PAPSS2).
checks.evidence_quote: We identified two orthologous genes, ATPSK2 and Atpsk2, encoding novel ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase orthologues in the respective regions of the human and mouse genomes.
checks.explanation: The paper identifies the human and mouse genes as orthologues.

checks.claim: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) showed that the brachymorphic (bm) mouse carries a missense mutation in the region of Atpsk2 (Papss2) that encodes the APS kinase activity.
checks.evidence_quote: a missense mutation in the region of Atpsk2 encoding the APS kinase activity in the brachymorphic mouse
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.
